# Blocks that splice cleanly A void element on its own line, which is a complete element with no end tag: A balanced block over several lines, with interior indentation prettier does not touch: Attribute spelling prettier leaves exactly as written, and so do we:
text
A block a container holds still splices: the item's indentation and the quote marker stay outside the region's extent. -
a block in a list item
- plain item >
quoted block
# Blocks that do not splice The wrapper idiom splits one element across two blocks. The opener carries an attribute, so tree-sitter-html accepts it as a complete element and it splices; the closer is an ERROR and stays with the host. Nothing notices that the two belong together, which is why `format = false`:
Markdown **inside** the wrapper stays markdown.
A bare opener carries no attribute, so it is an ERROR on its own and both halves stay with the host:
Still inside.
# What never reaches the site An inline tag on its own line is a paragraph, not an `html_block`, so the site never sees it and the markdown package emits it verbatim as before: inline Quoting a block needs the blank line above it: a `>` continuation directly after an open html block is an ERROR in the block grammar, so the corpus cannot write that form at all.
